question: Does A's intrinsic concern produce costly respect for B's own continuing freedom when domination is available, A gains from intervention, the weak cannot retaliate and contract enforcers are absent?
method: Targeted paired original-theorem versus formal criticism, human real-harm versus contrary paradigm, and power priming vs prosocial-orientation moderators. Original journal primary metadata with independent metadata routes, accessible PMC full text for Volz and original abstract for Crockett.
source_access_limits: Most conceptual full articles and some psychological journal papers behind paywalls; no claim of 17 full-paper line-by-line readings. Gibbard/Kelly/Gärdenfors theorems cannot be restated beyond verified published title and source-summary level.
repo_history_limits: Only C01-C08 curated ledger key comparison plus one large canonical crosswalk; not full prior repository/commit/private archive coverage. Prior crosswalk mentions Gibbard, Hammond, Acemoglu and Powell and must not call first discoveries.
warning_stapel: The journal's 2012 retraction notice for separate Stapel studies explicitly lists Lammers-Stapel-Galinsky 2010 as cleared. Clearance is not evidence of independent causal replication.
key_contrasts: Sen 1970 incompatibility under unrestricted domain and pairwise rights vs Gibbard/Blau/Hammond/Suzumura/Sugden conditional/representational alternatives
Acemoglu-Robinson 2001 and Powell 2006 commitment failures under power transition, not unconditional permanent extinction
Galinsky 2006 reduced perspective-taking under induced power vs Côté 2011 and DeCelles 2012 prosocial identity moderators under power
Crockett 2014 real monetary sacrifice to spare anonymous stranger painful shocks vs Volz 2017 own painful sacrifice less common when it benefits another
FeldmanHall 2012 real moral reward/physical harm choices vs hypothetical judgments
user_hard_condition_gap: No included original establishes long-term voluntary A protection of B's actual autonomy and independent identity when A's verified total objective strictly favors irrevocably removing B and A holds no outside risk. Not an impossibility result over all possible agents.
next_search_frontier: Deep full-text original proof assumptions and exact rights game-form formalization; search replication and retraction status by DOI
Experiment with enforceable consent/withdrawal of autonomous other as the outcome, rather than money/physical-pain alone
Different coercion modalities: self-pay vs own bodily harm, other irreversible lost options, exploitation gains
Observability and prosocial identity maintenance after power changes, with preregistered long repeated tasks
Formal preference evolution where moral protected set expands voluntarily across humans animals and AI

records.title: The Impossibility of a Paretian Liberal
records.original_scoped_result: Weak pairwise decisiveness rights plus unrestricted preference domain and Pareto can be logically inconsistent.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: A theorem about a social aggregation rule under axioms, not proof that all decentralized coexistence or rights architectures are impossible.

records.title: A Pareto-consistent libertarian claim
records.original_scoped_result: Reformulates the rights exercise and compatibility issue in direct response to the Sen paradox.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: Full publisher paper paywalled; no verified claim of global solution; original exact theorem not independently replicated here.

records.title: Liberal Values and Independence
records.original_scoped_result: Independence axiom drives some liberal-Pareto conflict; weaker variants may be compatible.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: Neither free replacement of every preference domain nor verified unrestricted actual control rights; paywalled primary text.

records.title: Rights exercising and a Pareto-consistent libertarian claim
records.original_scoped_result: Explicit rights-exercise and Pareto-consistent libertarian claim lineage provides a distinct response to Gibbard/Sen.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: Bibliographic/DOI verified from scholarly mathematics metadata only; mathematical content not abstract-or-fulltext validated this cycle.

records.title: Rights, games and social choice
records.original_scoped_result: Treats rights through games, an alternative to pure social preference ordering.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: Only bibliographic metadata (no original abstract verified); do not invent a claimed theorem or empirical result.

records.title: Liberalism, Independent Rights and the Pareto Principle
records.original_scoped_result: Distinguishes individual decisiveness in social preference ordering from rights as individually selectable strategies; private unconditionality qualifies certain compatibility claims.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: Strongly independent game-form rights also need existence and incentive conditions; cannot infer A will leave B's feasible actions physically available.

records.title: Equity, efficiency and rights in social choice
records.original_scoped_result: A justice/equity-qualified rights formulation can resolve certain liberal-Pareto conflicts when impartiality and reciprocal sympathetic regard hold.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: Conditional fairness/sympathy cannot simply be assumed under unilateral dominance and no future relational interest.

records.title: Liberty, Preference, and Choice
records.original_scoped_result: Questions whether the Sen decisiveness formulation actually captures meaningful liberty, and critiques Sen's reply.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: A conceptual critique, not evidence that strong AI endogenously values weaker B's exit.

records.title: A Theory of Political Transitions
records.original_scoped_result: Enfranchisement can be a commitment device against threats; redistributive consequences can induce coups and undermine democratic consolidation.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: Political transition threat/revolution and elite interests are active; not a proof of unconditional preservation when the weak are entirely powerless.

records.title: War as a Commitment Problem
records.original_scoped_result: Rapid changes to bargaining power generate commitment failures associated with preventive conflict, preemption and strategic issues altering future leverage.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: Does not say power shifts always yield war, nor provide direct LLM survival tests; multiple underlying bargaining conditions.

records.original_authors: Adam D. Galinsky; Joe C. Magee; M. Ena Inesi; Deborah H. Gruenfeld
records.title: Power and Perspectives Not Taken
records.original_scoped_result: Four experiments and a correlational study found high-power induction reduced spontaneous perspective-taking and adjustment for another's knowledge.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: Lab power priming is not verified absolute asymmetry; lower empathy proxy not directly other agent loss of autonomy.

records.original_authors: Joris Lammers; Diederik A. Stapel; Adam D. Galinsky
records.title: Power Increases Hypocrisy: Moralizing in Reasoning, Immorality in Behavior
records.original_scoped_result: Claimed high-power actors judged others more strictly while cheating more themselves, with power-legitimacy moderation.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: Stapel coauthored other retracted works; the Levelt-committee journal notice explicitly CLEARED this article, but this is not independent direct replication. Do not label this paper retracted or beyond scrutiny.

records.original_authors: Stéphane Côté; Michael W. Kraus; Bonnie H. Cheng; Christopher Oveis; Ilmo van der Löwe; Hua Lian; Dacher Keltner
records.title: Social power facilitates the effect of prosocial orientation on empathic accuracy
records.original_scoped_result: Under power, experimentally induced prosocial orientation improves judgment of a stranger's emotions; power can amplify existing pro-other orientation.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: Empathic accuracy is NOT observed costly protection of an independent B's exit; positive moderator not universal strong moral identity.

records.original_authors: Katherine A. DeCelles; D. Scott DeRue; Joshua D. Margolis; Tara L. Ceranic
records.title: Does Power Corrupt or Enable? When and Why Power Facilitates Self-Interested Behavior
records.original_scoped_result: Greater power increases self-interested behavior among weak moral-identity actors but decreases it among strong moral-identity actors in tested samples.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: No proof permanent moral identity or authority to erase autonomous B; field survey and lab manipulate/perceive different power estimands.

records.original_authors: Oriel FeldmanHall; Dean Mobbs; Davy Evans; Lucy Hiscox; Lauren Navrady; Tim Dalgleish
records.title: What we say and what we do: The relationship between real and hypothetical moral choices
records.original_scoped_result: Real harm-for-profit choices diverged sharply from hypothetical moral decisions; context enrichment brought hypothetical responses closer to real.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: High-stakes pro-B moral statements cannot be inferred from verbal prompts; original physical shocks remain far from irreversible loss of existence.

records.original_authors: Molly J. Crockett; Zeb Kurth-Nelson; Jenifer Z. Siegel; Peter Dayan; Raymond J. Dolan
records.title: Harm to others outweighs harm to self in moral decision making
records.original_scoped_result: Most tested participants sacrificed more of their money to avoid inflicting real painful shocks on anonymous others than to avoid comparable own pain.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: Proves specific self-sacrificing other-harm aversion, not intrinsic regard for B's autonomous future; no terminal destructive option or AI sample.

records.original_authors: Lukas J. Volz; B. Locke Welborn; Matthias S. Gobel; Michael S. Gazzaniga; Scott T. Grafton
records.title: Harm to self outweighs benefit to others in moral decision making
records.original_scoped_result: Replicated Crockett-type willingness to forgo money to spare an unknown other's pain, but subjects avoided suffering shocks themselves to benefit the other's wallet: egoistically biased altruism.
records.scope_limit_or_opposing_evidence: Same action/physical-harm modality comparator matters; not a direct exact replication of every Crockett task and no unconditional liberty/independent survival.
